summary: Iteration 5 checked that the PPT generates correctly and that the public site displays properly. PPT generation passed: gemini ppt_outline in English took 25s and produced 10 slides, 2 mermaid blocks, 5 [IMAGE] hooks with concrete subjects, no LaTeX, Unicode CO₂/C₆H₁₂O₆/H₂O, citations, and validation passed. The export smoke test found real Wikimedia images for all 5 hooks. The deck was converted with LibreOffice and rendered as a contact sheet: every slide has a title, bullets, and either an image, a diagram panel or full-width bullets. There is no overflow and captions are present. The renderMermaidPng logic in Chromium (htmlLabels false) made PNGs for both mermaid blocks with no foreignObject: 720x1078 and 1872x226. With those PNGs passed as assets.diagrams, slides 4 and 6 show pictures instead of text boxes. Website on :3005 at desktop 1920x800 and mobile 390x844 (/, /login, /signup): no console errors, no 4xx responses, no broken images, no horizontal overflow, fonts loaded, correct title. All role cards select on both forms. Links work: Get Started, Sign In, Start Creating, Create Free Account, Sign up, Sign in. All 9 protected routes return 307 to /login?next=... Regression: npm test 38/38, tsc 0 errors, lint 0 errors (4 warnings), HTTP pytest 33/33. A code review of the signed-in pages found a mobile overflow bug on /professor/generate (reproduced in a scratch page) and 'destructive' colours that are green.

minor.issue: Very wide images are placed at their natural aspect ratio in the right panel, so they become unreadable thin strips. Examples: the LR mermaid PNG on slide 6 (1872x226) and the Wikimedia 'photosynthesis chemical equation' image on slide 8. Fix: when the aspect ratio is over about 2.5, place the picture full-width under the bullets (or use a short bullet column with a wide image), or render LR flowcharts as TD.
Image captions in the PPTX are very small (about 7pt) and light grey, so they are barely readable when projected. Consider 9-10pt.

ui_bugs.issue: Below lg the grid has no template columns, so it uses an implicit 'auto' track and the grid items have no min-w-0. Wide content in the results card stretches the whole page on mobile; a scratch reproduction at 390px went to 1018px. Triggers are a code block (GeneratedContent uses [&_pre]:whitespace-pre), the mermaid-source fallback <pre>, a wide SVG, or a wide markdown table. With min-w-0 on the grid items the width stays at 390. Fix: use 'grid grid-cols-1 gap-6 lg:grid-cols-2' or add min-w-0 to both children. The same pattern is in professor/share (line 297) and student/notifications (line 81).

--destructive is set to green (148 42% 27%). Every 'text-destructive' looks green: error messages (admin-users-error, student dashboard alerts, notifications loadError), Trash icons, and the failing NEP score in admin/metrics line 155. A failing score there looks almost the same as a passing one (text-accent green). Use a red hue, e.g. 0 72% 45%.
/favicon.ico returns 404. There is no public/ folder and no app/icon file, so browser tabs show the default icon.

issues: No web font is loaded; the body uses the Tailwind system-ui stack. This is acceptable, but next/font (e.g. Inter or Noto Sans with Devanagari/Bengali/Telugu subsets) would make the look consistent across operating systems.
app-nav wraps <Button> inside <Link>, which nests interactive elements (a > button). This is an accessibility issue; use <Button asChild><Link/></Button>.
Looked fine. The faint horizontal banding in the JPEG screenshots is compression of the subtle from-background to-card gradient, not a CSS defect.

(Medium) globals.css: make --destructive red in :root, .dark and .dashboard-shell so errors and failing scores are visually distinct from success.
(Low) In addDeckSlide, give very wide pictures (aspect ratio over 2.5) a full-width layout below the bullets, or render LR mermaid as TD, so slide 6 and slide 8 are readable.

critical_code_review_comments: renderMermaidPng returns null for any error, including a tainted canvas, and the caller falls back to text. That is correct, but consider logging the reason with console.warn so it can be debugged.

Mermaid blocks with repeated node IDs and different labels (e.g. E["Calvin Cycle (Light-Independent)"] and later E["Calvin Cycle"]) silently use the last label. The generation guide could ask the model to define each node label once.
generate/page.tsx is 513 lines; consider splitting the results panel into its own component.

rca of the issue: Mobile overflow: CSS grid with no grid-template-columns creates an implicit 'auto' column. Grid items default to min-width:auto, so their min-content width includes nested scroll containers (pre with overflow-x:auto, or a wide SVG). The column grows past the viewport. Tailwind's grid-cols-1 (minmax(0,1fr)) or min-w-0 on the items clamps it. Verified with a scratch reproduction: 1018px wide becomes 390px.
